app.name.note: The product name, in the browser tab and in e-mails. Not translated.

sign-in.title.note: The sign-in page's heading and browser tab title. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

sign-in.email.note: Label of the e-mail address field on the sign-in page.

sign-in.password.note: Label of the password field on the sign-in page.

sign-in.failed.note: Heading of the box at the top of the sign-in page that says why signing in didn't work.

sign-in.incorrect.note: After a sign-in with a wrong e-mail address or password. It never says which, so it doesn't reveal whether an address has an account (ADR-0010 §2).

sign-in.unverified.note: After a sign-in with the right password, to an account whose e-mail address hasn't been confirmed with the link we e-mailed.

sign-in.wait-seconds.note: After repeated failed sign-ins, the next attempt has to wait (ADR-0010 §2). {count} is the number of seconds. Calm and factual: it never blames.

sign-in.wait-minutes.note: As sign-in.wait-seconds, for waits of a minute or more. {count} is the number of minutes, rounded up.

security.title.note: Heading of the security page, where a member sees and signs out their devices (ADR-0010 §6).

security.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the security page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

security.devices.note: Heading of the list of devices the account is signed in on.

security.device.note: A signed-in device. {browser} and {system} are names such as Firefox and Android, not translated.

security.unknown-browser.note: Stands in for {browser} in security.device when the browser isn't known; starts the sentence.

security.unknown-system.note: Stands in for {system} in security.device when the operating system isn't known; mid-sentence.

security.unknown-device.note: A signed-in device whose browser and system are both unknown.

security.this-device.note: Marks the device the member is using right now in the list of signed-in devices.

security.used-today.note: When a signed-in device was last used, within the last day. Exact to a day only.

security.used-days.note: When a signed-in device was last used. {count} is whole days ago, at least 1.

security.sign-out.note: Button next to each signed-in device that signs it out; next to this device, it signs the member out here.

security.sign-out-others.note: Button that signs out every device but the one in use.

security.signed-out.note: Status message after signing out another device.

security.signed-out-others.note: Status message after signing out all other devices.

security.not-found.note: Status message when the device to sign out was signed out already, for example from another tab.

security.passkeys.note: Heading of the security page's list of passkeys (ADR-0010 §2). Passkey is the common word in both languages.

security.passkeys-intro.note: Explains what a passkey is, in one line.

security.no-passkeys.note: Shown instead of the list when the account has no passkeys.

security.added-today.note: When a passkey was added less than a day ago.

security.added-days.note: When a passkey was added, in whole days; {count} is at least 1.

security.add-passkey.note: Button that starts adding a passkey; the browser then asks for the fingerprint, face or screen lock.

security.remove-passkey.note: Button next to a passkey that removes it. Its device name is read with it.

security.passkey-added.note: Status message after a passkey was added.

security.passkey-removed.note: Status message after a passkey was removed.

security.passkey-not-found.note: Status message when the passkey to remove was already gone.

security.passkey-failed.note: When the browser or the server couldn't add the passkey, for instance because it was cancelled.

security.confirm.note: Heading of the step that asks for the password again before passkeys can change (ADR-0010 §6).

security.confirm-intro.note: Why the password is asked again: the sign-in is over 10 minutes old.

security.confirm-password.note: Label of the password field when confirming it's you.

security.confirm-submit.note: Button that confirms with the password.

security.confirm-failed.note: Heading of the box that says why confirming didn't work.

security.incorrect-password.note: When the password typed to confirm is wrong.

security.confirmed.note: Status message after confirming: changes are possible for 10 minutes.

email.password-reset.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail with a link to choose a new password (ADR-0010 §8). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.password-reset.request.note: First line of the password reset e-mail. It doesn't say who asked: anyone can ask for any address.

email.password-reset.action.note: Text of the link in the password reset e-mail, and the label before the link in its plain-text part.

email.password-reset.expiry.note: Says how long the reset link works (ADR-0010 §8: once, for 30 minutes).

email.password-reset.not-you.note: Last line of the password reset e-mail, for someone who didn't ask. Calm: nothing happens unless the link is used.

email.password-changed.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent after a password was changed through a reset link (ADR-0010 §8). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.password-changed.done.note: First line of the password-changed e-mail: what happened, including that every device was signed out.

email.password-changed.not-you.note: For someone who didn't change it: their mailbox is the way in. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.passkey-added.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when a passkey was added to the account (ADR-0010 §2, ADR-0014 §2). Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.passkey-added.done.note: First line of the passkey-added e-mail: what happened, and what a passkey can do.

email.passkey-added.not-you.note: For someone who didn't add it: someone else is signed in. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

email.passkey-removed.subject.note: Subject of the e-mail sent when a passkey was removed from the account. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

email.passkey-removed.done.note: First line of the passkey-removed e-mail.

email.passkey-removed.not-you.note: For someone who didn't remove it. The quoted text is the sign-in page's link, sign-in.forgot-password, and must match it.

sign-in.forgot-password.note: Link on the sign-in page to ask for a password reset. The password-changed e-mail quotes it, so keep both the same.

sign-in.password-changed.note: Status message on the sign-in page after a new password was saved.

forgot.title.note: Heading of the page to ask for a link to choose a new password (ADR-0010 §8).

forgot.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the forgotten-password page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

forgot.email.note: Label of the e-mail address field on the forgotten-password page.

forgot.submit.note: Button that asks for the reset link.

forgot.sent.note: After asking for a link. It never says whether {email}, the address typed, has an account (ADR-0010 §2).

forgot.failed.note: Heading of the box that says why asking for a link didn't work.

forgot.invalid.note: When what was typed isn't an e-mail address. The example address is an invented one.

reset.title.note: Heading of the page reached from the reset link, to choose a new password.

reset.page-title.note: Browser tab title of the new-password page. Householdr is the product name, not translated.

reset.password.note: Label of the new password field.

reset.hint.note: Hint under the new password field (ADR-0010 §2: at least 12 characters, no composition rules).

reset.submit.note: Button that saves the new password.

reset.failed.note: Heading of the box that says why saving the new password didn't work.

reset.too-short.note: When the new password has fewer than 12 characters.

reset.too-long.note: When the new password has more than 128 characters.

reset.breached.note: When the new password is in Have I Been Pwned's list of breached passwords (ADR-0010 §2). Calm: it says why, without blame.

reset.expired.note: When the reset link was used already, is older than 30 minutes, or isn't one.

reset.ask-again.note: Link to the forgotten-password page, after an expired link.
